title_en: Continuation Vehicles from the LP Seat – Scott Ramsower (EP.523)
title_zh: 从 LP 席位看延续载体——Scott Ramsower（Texas Teachers / ILPA）EP.523
subtitle_zh: Texas Teachers 私募股权掌门、ILPA 董事会主席剖析 LP 警惕延续载体的十大原因、僵尸基金与零售资本隐忧。
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 由 Ted Seides 对话 Scott Ramsower——Teachers' Retirement System of Texas（德州教师退休系统）私募股权负责人，在这个规模 2500 亿美元的养老金内管理私募股权组合，16 年间把团队从 6 人、70 亿美元带到 27 人、330 亿美元，同时担任机构有限合伙人协会（ILPA）董事会主席。核心议题是从 LP 席位审视延续载体（continuation vehicle, CV，即延续基金、GP 主导二手份额）：他直言 CV 本身无所谓好坏、每个都需单独审视，但近年 LP 的沮丧达到新高，甚至有人戏称 CV 为冲突载体（conflict vehicle）。他系统剖析 LP 警惕 CV 的十大原因，从利益冲突的定价、错位的经济条款到右尾收益（right-tail）的流失与跟投的自我蚕食。以定价为例：GP 以 100 美元买入的资产以 300 美元卖给 CV，成本基础被抬高，LP 付的 70 个基点看似低于 1%，实则高于原来 100 美元上的 100 个基点。他也谈到 ILPA 的 CV 最佳实践清单（理由、流程、定价等）、僵尸基金，以及零售资本的隐忧——对零售投资人而言私募股权是对的策略、错的结构。是一集从出资人视角拆解 GP 主导二级市场的深谈。
description: Continuation Vehicles from the LP Seat – Scott Ramsower (EP.523)

turns.en: Continuation vehicles, continuation funds, GP led secondaries, I'm a strong believer that they're neither inherently good or inherently bad.
turns.zh: 延续载体（continuation vehicle）、延续基金（continuation fund）、GP 主导二手份额（GP-led secondaries）——我坚信它们本身无所谓好坏。

turns.en: Each vehicle is unique and bespoke and requires examination on its own. With that comes some difficulties. If you go back when CVs took off the second wave 10 years ago, GPs treated it like a new invention.
turns.zh: 每个载体都是独特、定制的，需要单独审视。随之而来也有一些困难。把时间拨回十年前 CV 第二波兴起的时候，GP 们把它当成一项新发明。

turns.en: Historically, there's been three ways to exit a business. An IPO, a sale to a sponsor, or a sale to a strategic. All of a sudden, we had invented this fourth way.
turns.zh: 历史上，退出一个企业有三种方式：IPO、出售给财务买家（sponsor），或者出售给战略买家。突然之间，我们发明了第四种方式。

turns.en: You would think LPs would be super excited by this, and GPs were. They were metaphorically high-fiving each other because they had just increased the exit routes by a third.
turns.zh: 你可能以为 LP 们会为此兴奋不已，GP 们确实很兴奋。他们仿佛在互相击掌，因为他们刚刚把退出路径增加了三分之一。

turns.en: As I looked around and evaluated these on my own, as our team evaluated them, as I talked to my fellow LPs, it quickly became apparent that LPs were not nearly as enthusiastic as GPs expected them to be.
turns.zh: 但当我自己观察评估、当我们团队评估、当我和其他 LP 交流时，很快就发现，LP 远没有 GP 预期的那么热情。

turns.en: Recently, I've seen frustrations hit new highs. I chair the board of ILPA. I spend a lot of time with some of the senior-most LPs in this industry.
turns.zh: 最近，我看到这种沮丧达到了新高。我担任 ILPA 的董事会主席，和这个行业里最资深的一些 LP 有大量接触。

turns.en: When I hear things like, CVs are the bane of my existence. There's a joke now that CV stands for conflict vehicle. Some LPs say my heart sinks when a CV request lands in my inbox.
turns.zh: 当我听到类似'CV 是我存在的克星'这样的话——现在有个玩笑说 CV 代表 conflict vehicle（冲突载体）。有些 LP 说，CV 请求一进收件箱，我的心就往下沉。

turns.en: I've even heard some say CVs are going to be the death of the industry. I'm Ted Sides, and this is Capital Allocators. My guest on today's show is Scott Ramsauer, head of private equity funds at the teacher retirement system of Texas, where he oversees the private equity portfolio inside a $250 billion pension plan.
turns.zh: 我甚至听有人说 CV 会毁灭这个行业。我是 Ted Seides，这里是 Capital Allocators。今天节目的嘉宾是 Scott Ramsower，Teachers' Retirement System of Texas（德州教师退休系统）的私募股权基金负责人，他在一个 2500 亿美元的养老金计划内管理私募股权组合。

turns.en: Scott joined Texas teachers 16 years ago and has been instrumental in the private equity program's growth from six people and $7 billion in assets to 27 people and $33 billion today.
turns.zh: Scott 16 年前加入 Texas Teachers，在私募股权项目从 6 个人、70 亿美元资产增长到今天的 27 个人、330 亿美元的过程中发挥了关键作用。

turns.en: He also chairs the board of ILPA, the Institutional Limited Partners Association. Our conversation covers Scott's path from equity research to the LP seat and the growth of the private equity program at TRS.
turns.zh: 他还担任 ILPA——机构有限合伙人协会（Institutional Limited Partners Association）——的董事会主席。我们的对话涵盖 Scott 从股票研究到 LP 席位的路径，以及 TRS 私募股权项目的成长。

turns.en: We cover the many reasons LPs are wary of continuation vehicles from conflictive pricing and misaligned economics to the loss of the right tail, best practices for CVs, zombie funds, retail capital and private equity, and the new demands created by the current challenging environment.
turns.zh: 我们还谈到了 LP 警惕延续载体的诸多原因——从利益冲突的定价、错位的经济条款，到右尾收益的流失；以及 CV 的最佳实践、僵尸基金、零售资本与私募股权，还有当前艰难环境带来的新要求。

turns.en: Scott, good to see you. Good to see you, Ted. I know we're gonna talk a lot about continuation funds. Why don't we start with your background and path to the seat?
turns.zh: Scott，很高兴见到你。——很高兴见到你，Ted。我知道我们会聊很多延续基金的话题。我们不如先从你的背景和进入 LP 席位的路径聊起？

turns.en: Born and raised in Texas. I went to university in Texas. Had an internship at Enron. The summer that it all went wrong. Had an incredible experience, had an offer, but decided I wanted to move to New York.
turns.zh: 在德州出生长大，在德州读的大学。在 Enron 实习过——就在一切崩塌的那个夏天。那是一次很棒的经历，也拿到了录用，但我决定搬去纽约。

turns.en: I wanted to work on Wall Street. I turned it down. I'm glad I did because by the end of that year, Enron was no more. That was a formidable experience for me.
turns.zh: 我想在华尔街工作，所以拒绝了它。我很庆幸这么做了，因为那年年底，Enron 就不复存在了。那对我是一堂令人警醒的课。

turns.en: I wanted to be a stock picker. I interviewed around, I networked, I got an offer with Morgan Stanley to join their equity research team. This was in the fall of 2001.
turns.zh: 我想做选股。我到处面试、到处经营人脉，拿到了 Morgan Stanley 股票研究团队的录用。那是 2001 年秋天。

turns.en: The dot com bubble had just burst. Around Christmas break, I got a call saying, unfortunately, massive layoffs, the economy's not good. We can no longer honor that offer.
turns.zh: 互联网泡沫刚刚破裂。圣诞节放假期间，我接到一个电话说：很不幸，大规模裁员，经济形势不好，我们没法兑现那份录用。

turns.en: I said, oh, I was looking forward to having fun my last semester in college and now I'm jobless. I moved to New York and I joined the litigation consulting business of PWC.
turns.zh: 我说，哦，我还盼着开开心心过完大学的最后一个学期，现在却失业了。我搬去纽约，加入了 PwC 的诉讼咨询业务。

turns.en: I'd got to see a lot of interesting frauds as a forensic accountant. I always had at the back of my head this itch to get back and be a stock picker.
turns.zh: 作为法务会计师，我见识了许多有意思的欺诈案。但我心里始终有一个痒处——想回去做选股。

turns.en: Lo and behold, 2004, came around. Two years later, I got a call back from Morgan Stanley. They said, market's different. Can we talk? I got an offer, I joined Morgan Stanley.
turns.zh: 果不其然，2004 年来了，两年之后 Morgan Stanley 给我回了电话，说市场不一样了，能聊聊吗？我拿到录用，加入了 Morgan Stanley。

turns.en: They stuck the Texan on the energy team. I grew up in suburban Dallas, Texas, never seen the oil well in my life. I loved it. That's how I got into investing.
turns.zh: 他们把这个德州人塞进了能源团队。我在达拉斯郊区长大，这辈子没见过油井。我爱上了这份工作。我就是这么进入投资领域的。

turns.en: Quickly over the course of my two years as a stock picker, I realized three key things. First, I quickly realized I wanted to be on the buy side, not the sell side.
turns.zh: 在两年的选股师生涯里，我很快意识到三件关键的事。第一，我很快发现自己想待在买方，而不是卖方。

turns.en: I wanted to be making investments, not making investment recommendations. The second one, I decided public markets may not be for me. I would get in early, work all hours, end of the night, early morning, submit a final research report after the earnings came out to my boss.
turns.zh: 我想做投资，而不是做投资建议。第二，我判断公开市场也许不适合我。我会很早进场，没日没夜地工作，财报发布后连夜把最终研究报告发给老板。

turns.en: We'd publish our report, nobody cared. The market had moved hours and hours before. I quickly realized I'm more of a longer term, fundamentals type investor, which to me signaled private equity might be the right way to go.
turns.zh: 我们发布报告，没人理会。市场在几个小时前就已经动完了。我很快意识到自己是更偏长线、基本面型的投资人，这让我觉得私募股权也许才是对的方向。

turns.en: The third piece I had to figure out is, did I want to be a GP or an LP? And this was in 2006. The LP industry was much smaller than it is today.
turns.zh: 第三件要想清楚的是：我想做 GP 还是 LP？那是 2006 年，LP 行业比今天小得多。

turns.en: I started doing as much research as I could. I started networking with as many people as I could. I learned a lot about LPs and what they do.
turns.zh: 我开始尽可能多做研究，尽可能多地去认识人。我学到了很多关于 LP 和他们工作的知识。

turns.en: I knew what GPs were. I lived in New York. I had roommates that worked at GPs. This is neither good or bad. I call a GP an inch wide and a mile deep.
turns.zh: 我知道 GP 是干什么的——我住在纽约，室友就在 GP 工作。这无所谓好坏。我说 GP 是一英寸宽、一英里深。

turns.en: The more I learned about LPs, I decided they're an inch deep and a mile wide. For me and my own interest, skill sets and intellectual curiosity, that sounded pretty interesting.
turns.zh: 对 LP 了解越多，我越觉得他们是'一英寸深、一英里宽'。就我个人的兴趣、技能组合和求知欲而言，这听起来相当有意思。

turns.en: I interviewed with anyone that I could, ultimately got a job with Alpenvest partners. I spent four years with Alpenvest, learned everything there is to know about being a private equity LP, fell in love with the LP side of things.
turns.zh: 我尽可能到处面试，最终加入了 AlpInvest Partners。我在 AlpInvest 待了四年，学到了做私募股权 LP 该会的一切，也爱上了 LP 这一边。

turns.en: I also met a woman along the way. We got married while we lived up here in New York. She happened to be a fellow Texan. After spending eight years in the Northeast, both of us looked around, said what do we want to do at this next phase and where do we want to plan our routes?
turns.zh: 一路上我还遇到了一位女士。我们住在纽约时结了婚，她恰好也是德州人。在东北部待了八年后，我们互相看了看，说下一阶段想做什么、想在哪里规划人生？

turns.en: We decided for us that was going to be back home. In 2010, we packed up, left the city, moved to Austin, Texas, and I linked up with the teacher retirement system of Texas where I am to this day.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，答案是回家。2010 年我们收拾行囊离开纽约，搬到德州奥斯汀，我加入了 Teachers' Retirement System of Texas，一直待到今天。

turns.en: I've been at TRS or Texas teachers for 16 and a half years. I focused exclusively on private equity. When I joined, the private equity portfolio was six people, seven billion of NAV approximately.
turns.zh: 我在 TRS——Texas Teachers——已经 16 年半了，专注私募股权。我加入时，私募股权组合大约 6 个人、70 亿美元的净值（NAV）。

turns.en: Fast forward over 16 years later, we're now 27 investment professionals on the private equity team, about 33 billion in NAV and private equity.
turns.zh: 一晃 16 多年过去，如今私募股权团队有 27 位投资专业人士，私募股权 NAV 约 330 亿美元。

turns.en: It's been a fun ride. It's been a great time to be an LP in this industry. Today, I lead the private equity funds team within Texas teachers.
turns.zh: 这一路很有趣，在这个行业做 LP 赶上了好时候。今天，我领导 Texas Teachers 内部的私募股权基金团队。

turns.en: What are some of the key lessons or inflection points? The first one was coming out in the dot-com recession, having my dream job swept out from under my feet was a little bit of a blow to the ego, blow to the plan.
turns.zh: 有哪些关键的教训或转折点？第一个是在互联网泡沫衰退期出来时，梦想中的工作在脚下被抽走，对自尊、对人生规划都是一个小打击。

turns.en: I thought I had it all figured out. The world had a different plan for me. My lesson learned was that's okay. Life is sometimes not a straight line.
turns.zh: 我原以为自己把一切都想明白了，但世界给我安排了别的剧本。我学到的教训是：没关系，人生有时不是一条直线。

turns.en: It's a series of decisions. I still generated an incredible network from that first job, some great skills. I saw some cool stuff, a little bit of a different route than I had planned in my own head.
turns.zh: 它是一连串决定的组合。我从那份第一份工作里依然积累了可观的人脉和一些很棒的技能，见识了一些有意思的东西——和我脑子里规划的路径不太一样。

turns.en: The next key lesson was I was at Alpenvest, investing in private equity when the bubble burst in 2008 in the GFC. The lesson learned there was when others are pulling back, go in.
turns.zh: 下一个关键教训是在 AlpInvest 做私募股权投资时，遇上 2008 年全球金融危机泡沫破裂。那次的教训是：当别人退缩时，进场。

turns.en: 2009 ended up being an incredible vintage. 2010 was an incredible vintage, an incredible time to deploy capital. How about once you got in the seat taking a program from the size it was to the size of this today?
turns.zh: 2009 年结果成了了不起的年份，2010 年也是了不起的年份，是部署资本的绝佳时机。——那么，你坐上 LP 席位之后，把一个项目从当时的规模做到今天这个体量，又是什么体验？

turns.en: That's been a lesson in Rome wasn't built in a day. I look back and think about how much our program has evolved. I was just a small piece of that evolution.
turns.zh: 那是一堂'罗马非一日建成'的课。我回顾我们的项目演变到今天的样子，我只是那其中的一小部分。

turns.en: Never once did any of us sit down on the team and say, this is where we're gonna be in 16 years. This is what we're gonna do today. This is the next stop along our journey.
turns.zh: 我们团队从头到尾没有哪一次坐下来规划说：16 年后我们要到这里，今天做这件事，旅程下一站是那里。

turns.en: We'd accomplish that and then say, what's next? The Texas Teachers Program was built over a long period of time, one step at a time. As you look at your portfolio in the industry today, there's been this big exit bottleneck, continuation vehicles, perhaps not as well understood in the community as you would like.
turns.zh: 我们完成一个目标，然后问：下一步是什么？Texas Teachers 的项目是长期一步一个脚印建起来的。——看看你今天的组合和行业，出现了巨大的退出瓶颈——延续载体——大家对它的理解可能不如你希望的那么深。

turns.en: Would love to get your thoughts of, how did you come about thinking through all the challenges in understanding what a CV means to an LP? Continuation vehicles, continuation funds, GP led secondaries.
turns.zh: 很想听听你的想法：你是如何一步步思考这些挑战、理解 CV 对 LP 意味着什么的？延续载体、延续基金、GP 主导的二手份额——

turns.en: I'm a strong believer that they're neither inherently good or inherently bad. Each vehicle is unique and bespoke and requires examination on its own.
turns.zh: 我坚信它们本身无所谓好坏。每个载体都是独特、定制的，需要单独审视。

turns.en: With that comes some difficulties. If you go back when CVs took off the second wave 10 years ago, GPs treated it like a new invention. Historically, there's been three ways to exit a business.
turns.zh: 随之而来也有一些困难。把时间拨回十年前 CV 第二波兴起的时候，GP 们把它当成一项新发明。历史上，退出一个企业有三种方式：

turns.en: An IPO, a sale to a sponsor, or a sale to a strategic. All of a sudden, we had invented this fourth way. You would think LPs would be super excited by this, and GPs were.
turns.zh: IPO、出售给财务买家（sponsor），或者出售给战略买家。突然之间，我们发明了第四种方式。你可能以为 LP 们会为此兴奋不已，GP 们确实很兴奋。

turns.en: They were metaphorically high-fiving each other because they had just increased the exit routes by a third. As I looked around and evaluated these on my own, as our team evaluated them, as I talked to my fellow LPs, it quickly became apparent that LPs were not nearly as enthusiastic as GPs expected them to be.
turns.zh: 他们仿佛在互相击掌，因为他们刚刚把退出路径增加了三分之一。但当我自己观察评估、当我们团队评估、当我和其他 LP 交流时，很快就发现，LP 远没有 GP 预期的那么热情。

turns.en: Recently, I've seen frustrations hit new highs by Chair of the Board of ILPA. I spend a lot of time with some of the senior-most LPs in this industry.
turns.zh: 最近，我看到沮丧情绪达到了新高。我担任 ILPA 的董事会主席，和这个行业里最资深的一些 LP 有大量接触。

turns.en: When I hear things like, CVs are the bane of my existence. There's a joke now that CV stands for conflict vehicle. Some LPs say my heart sinks when a CV request lands in my inbox.
turns.zh: 当我听到类似'CV 是我存在的克星'这样的话——现在有个玩笑说 CV 代表 conflict vehicle（冲突载体）。有些 LP 说，CV 请求一进收件箱，我的心就往下沉。

turns.en: I've even heard some say CVs are going to be the death of the industry. These are strong statements that clearly are not high-fiving the GPs for creating this fourth exit tool.
turns.zh: 我甚至听有人说 CV 会毁灭这个行业。这些都是强烈的表态，显然不是在 GP 创造了第四种退出工具而跟他们击掌。

turns.en: I started to say, LPs have strong emotions about this. GPs are not fully appreciating the nuance of the concerns. I started to write down some ideas as to how to articulate why LPs can be concerned about this.
turns.zh: 我开始意识到：LP 对这件事有强烈的情绪，而 GP 并没有充分理解这些 concerns 的微妙之处。我开始写下一些想法，试图说清楚 LP 为什么会担忧。

turns.en: It started with the conflicted nature. That's where GPs thought that it started and ended. As I started jotting more and more down, I realized there's a lot more to this that GPs might value hearing beyond the conflicted nature of the transactions.
turns.zh: 它始于利益冲突的属性。GP 以为事情到利益冲突为止。但随着我越写越多，我意识到这背后还有很多东西——超越交易的冲突属性——GP 可能会觉得值得听。

turns.en: I've come up with the top 10 reasons. LPs are concerned about CVs. You and I were talking at a conference this summer and I mentioned it. Here we are.
turns.zh: 我总结出了 LP 担忧 CV 的前十大原因。今年夏天一个会议上我和你我聊起过这件事，提到了它。于是就有了今天。

turns.en: Let's have at it. We don't have Letterman anymore, so it'll be the Scott Graham Sauer top 10 list. We'll start with one and go up to 10. The first reason LPs are concerned are exactly what GPs expected.
turns.zh: 那我们这就开始。现在没有 Letterman 了，所以我们就来一份 Scott Ramsower 版十大清单，从第 1 条数到第 10 条。LP 担忧的第一个原因，恰恰是 GP 料到的那些。

turns.en: These are conflicted transaction. There's conflicted pricing. There's imperfect price discovery. The GPs sits on both sides of the trade. They act as the agent for the seller, which is the legacy LPs.
turns.zh: 这些是存在利益冲突的交易。定价是冲突的，价格发现不完备。GP 坐在交易的两边：他们充当卖方的代理人——卖方是原来的老 LP——

turns.en: Functionally, they also act as the agent for the buyer, which is the incoming CV investors. That makes it hard to know whether the price is real, whether a competitive process was run.
turns.zh: 实际上也充当买方的代理人——买方是新投入 CV 的投资人。这就很难判断价格是否真实、是否进行了竞争性的流程。

turns.en: That's the main and the original concern around LPs. Around CVs is the conflicted nature of the transaction. Before we move on, now that that's been in the market for a while, what do you see as best practices in an inherently opaque pricing environment?
turns.zh: 这就是 LP 对 CV 最主要的、最初的担忧——交易的利益冲突属性。——在往下走之前，既然这个机制在市场上已经存在一段时间了，在你看来，在这种本质上不透明的定价环境里，什么是最佳实践？

turns.en: ILPA has issued a two-dotto of continuation vehicle best practices. It's in the draft process, collecting community input, that comes down to four things.
turns.zh: ILPA 已经发布了一份延续载体最佳实践的待办清单，目前还在草案流程中征集社区意见，归结起来是四件事。

turns.en: One of which is pricing. The first is the rationale. Is there a genuine case that the CV is a deliberate solution, as opposed to a default? Is this the best option that exists?
turns.zh: 其中一件是定价。第一是理由：有没有真实的理由说明这个 CV 是一个深思熟虑的解决方案，而不是一个默认选项？这是不是现存的最佳选择？

turns.en: The second one is the process. Was a truly competitive auction run? Did third-party, non-secondary buyers participate? Was there a process to seek a wholesale sale of these assets?
turns.zh: 第二是流程：是否真正组织了竞争性的拍卖？有没有第三方、非二手份额的买家参与？有没有尝试过把这些资产整体出售？

turns.en: Is there full-price transparency around what the final bidders offered? For example, if one bidder is willing to pay 90 cents on the dollar for an asset, another bidder will pay 89 cents on the dollar, but commit to the GP's next fund.
turns.zh: 对最终出价有没有完整的价格透明度？比如，一个买家愿意为一项资产付出每美元 90 美分，另一个愿意出 89 美分，但承诺投资 GP 的下一期基金。

turns.en: That's something LPs don't always have transparency into. Usually the LPAC just says, this is the bid we've decided to go with. LPs are now requesting more transparency to prove, is there more to the bid than just the headline pricing?
turns.zh: 这种东西 LP 往往看不到全貌。通常 LP 咨询委员会只会说，这是我们决定接受的报价。现在 LP 在要求更高的透明度以验证：除了报价头数之外，出价背后还有没有别的东西？

turns.en: In addition to support the valuation as a third-party fairness opinion, a lot of LPs say that those can have limited value. They're a important process check.
turns.zh: 此外，作为估值的支撑，要有第三方的公平意见书（fairness opinion）。很多 LP 说它的价值有限，但它是一个重要的流程检查。

turns.en: Through it all, finally checking in on governance and alignment, do the LPs get sufficient time to review the roll or sell decision? Are LPs economically neutral, meaning that they're no worse off from an economics perspective?
turns.zh: 贯穿始终的，最后是治理和利益对齐的检查：LP 是否有足够时间审阅滚入还是卖出的决定？LP 在经济条款上是否保持中立——也就是从经济角度不会变差？

turns.en: Is the GP rolling its own carry? Full transparency into the alignment. If you look at the totality of CVs that you've seen in your seat, do you find the pricing fair in general?
turns.zh: GP 是否在滚入自己的 carry？对齐情况是否完全透明？——如果你看看在你这个席位上见过的所有 CV，你总体上觉得定价公平吗？

turns.en: Is there a wide dispersion, heavily discounted? What should you expect when a CV lands on your desk? It's a complicated transaction. Every time we're talking about these internally, I'm learning something new.
turns.zh: 是否存在很大的分化、大幅的折价？当一个 CV 落到你的桌上时，你应该预期什么？这是一笔复杂的交易。每次我们在内部讨论这些，我都在学到新东西。

turns.en: A lot of times the questions are similar. There's more bells and whistles getting added to all of these. Ilpa's trying to help and come out with a standardized checklist for the GP to fill out.
turns.zh: 很多时候问题是相似的，这些东西上加的花样也越来越多。ILPA 正试图帮忙，推出一份标准化的检查清单让 GP 逐项填写。

turns.en: Did you do X, did you do Y? Oftentimes, you have to peel back the onion. It's similar to a co-invest in a lot of ways. There's an asset, you have to form a view on that asset.
turns.zh: 你做没做 X？你做没做 Y？很多时候你得一层层剥洋葱。这在很多方面和跟投（co-invest）类似：有一项资产，你必须对这项资产形成观点。

turns.en: Is it an asset you wanna own or an asset you don't wanna own? On top of that, something you don't have to do in a co-investment, but you do have to do in a CV is determine alignment.
turns.zh: 这是你想拥有的资产，还是不想拥有的资产？除此之外，有些事在跟投里不需要做、但在 CV 里必须做，就是判断利益对齐。

turns.en: Almost always in a co-investment, you're fully aligned with the GP. You'll buy at the same terms, you'll sell at the same terms. If they win, you win.
turns.zh: 在跟投里，你几乎总是和 GP 完全对齐：同样的条款买入，同样的条款卖出。他们赢，你就赢。

turns.en: If you win, they win. That's not always the case with the CV. You have to understand where does the GP's alignment lie? What are they getting out of this transaction?
turns.zh: 你赢，他们也赢。CV 就未必如此了。你必须理解 GP 的利益对齐在哪里？他们从这笔交易里得到什么？

turns.en: What is the third-party offer? Is that a fair price? We start with the obvious one that is more complex than it seems on the surface. Why don't you bring me through the next nine?
turns.zh: 第三方的出价是什么？那是不是公允的价格？——我们从第一个原因开始，它比表面上看起来更复杂。带我过一遍后面的九个吧。

turns.en: Beyond conflicted pricing. Number two, dilution of GP mind share. Every hour a GP spends managing a CV is an hour they're not spending managing my commingled fund, the fund to which I committed capital.
turns.zh: 在冲突定价之外。第二个：GP 注意力（mind share）的稀释。GP 花在管理一个 CV 上的每一小时，都不是花在管理我的混合基金——我承诺出资的那只基金——上的时间。

turns.en: I may be an investor in that CV, but if I'm not, I'm losing their mind share. It's not a restricted only to CVs. There are other things that cause loss of GP mind share, but it's one of the reasons that LPs can be concerned about these.
turns.zh: 我可能是那个 CV 的投资人，但如果我不是，我就在失去他们的注意力。这并非 CV 独有，别的东西也会造成 GP 注意力的流失，但这是 LP 担忧它们的原因之一。

turns.en: The third reason would be dilution of alignment. A CV is a new economic vehicle that will bring in a new stream of revenues for management fees from Cary.
turns.zh: 第三个原因是利益对齐的稀释。CV 是一个新的经济载体，会管理费和管理费分成（carry）带来新的收入流。

turns.en: This opens the door for the GP to win even if the original fund loses. LPs are always trying to create scenarios of perfect alignment such that if LP loses, the GP loses and the LP wins, GP wins.
turns.zh: 这就给 GP 打开了一扇门：即使原基金输了，GP 也能赢。LP 一直在努力创造完全对齐的结构：LP 输 GP 就输，LP 赢 GP 才赢。

turns.en: Continuing on, the fourth, LPs can potentially be paying worse economics for a deal they already owned. LPs have to take the time and focus to ensure that the management fee rate is the same, the headline percentage, the cost basis is unchanged.
turns.zh: 继续。第四个：LP 可能为自己已经拥有的交易付出更差的经济条款。LP 必须花时间、集中精力确保管理费率相同——就是那个表面百分比——成本基础没有变化。

turns.en: Cary shouldn't be at a higher rate than you would have otherwise paid in the fund. Rolling into a new CV should not be paying more to own the same asset.
turns.zh: Carry 的费率不应高于你在原基金里本应支付的水平。滚入新的 CV，不应意味着为持有同样的资产付更多的钱。

turns.en: That's not always an easy calculation to do. The owners should be on the GP to ensure rolling LPs are no worse off. We call this an economic status quo.
turns.zh: 这笔账并不总是好算。责任应该在 GP：确保滚入的 LP 不吃亏，我们称之为经济状况持平（economic status quo）。

turns.en: What are some of the ways that an LP might not fully understand they're gonna be paying more rolling into a CV? Perfect example. Let's pretend we're in a fund after the investment period, the management fee is 100 basis points, 1% on invested capital.
turns.zh: LP 可能没有完全意识到滚入 CV 后自己要多付钱的例子有哪些？一个完美的例子：假设我们在一只已过投资期的基金里，管理费是 100 个基点，即已投资本的 1%。

turns.en: Let's pretend the asset that they're gonna sell to the CV they bought for $100. Us LPs would be paying 1% on $100 or $1 a year. The CV may have 70 basis points as a headline management fee rate.
turns.zh: 假设他们要卖给 CV 的那项资产当初是 100 美元买进的。我们这些 LP 付的是 100 美元的 1%，即一年 1 美元。CV 的名义管理费率可能是 70 个基点。

turns.en: 70 basis points, that's good, that's less than 1%. However, the second component of the management fee is crucial, which is what is the cost basis.
turns.zh: 70 个基点，听起来不错，低于 1%。然而管理费的第二部分才是关键：成本基础是什么。

turns.en: The GP may be bought the asset originally at $100. They're gonna sell it to the CV at $300. Your new cost basis is $300, but LP is now paying 70 basis points on $300, which is higher than 100 basis points on $100.
turns.zh: GP 当初可能以 100 美元买入该资产，要以 300 美元卖给 CV。你的新成本基础是 300 美元，于是 LP 现在付的是 300 美元上的 70 个基点——高于 100 美元上的 100 个基点。

turns.en: That's on the management fee. On the carry, the market can differ. Oftentimes there's tiered carry. We've seen structures such that carry can end up being higher than the original fund.
turns.zh: 这还只是管理费。在 carry 上，情况可能不同。常见的是分层 carry，我们见过一些结构，使得 carry 最终反而比原基金更高。

turns.en: The fifth one is more complex than a lot of realize. Many LPs don't have a choice to roll. While GPs present CVs as you make the call, stay or you can sell, it's your choice LPs.
turns.zh: 第五个比很多人意识到的更复杂：很多 LP 其实没有选择滚不滚。虽然 GP 把 CV 说成'你可以滚入、可以留下、也可以卖掉，是你的选择，LP'——

turns.en: A lot of LPs for a variety of reasons don't have that choice. They may have a board approval process that takes longer than the CV process allows for.
turns.zh: 但很多 LP 出于各种原因并没有那个选择。他们的董事会审批流程可能比 CV 流程允许的时间更长。

turns.en: They may have a legal review or no bandwidth from their legal team to do a legal review. The election windows oftentimes can be short 20 to 30 business days.
turns.zh: 他们可能有法律审查，或者法务团队没有带宽来做法律审查。选择窗口往往很短，20 到 30 个工作日。

turns.en: They might have a plate full of other priorities to get done while it's presented as a choice. A lot of LPs don't have a choice. As a result, their only option is to sell.
turns.zh: 他们手上可能还压着一堆别的优先事项。虽然表面上是个选择，很多 LP 其实没得选。结果是他们唯一的选项就是卖出。

turns.en: And that's concerning. The sixth one, CVs can artificially enhance fund metrics. The original commingled fund, when it sells a CV to a new vehicle, it produces DPI and an IRR for that fund.
turns.zh: 这令人担忧。第六个：CV 可以人为地美化基金的指标。原来的混合基金把资产卖给新的 CV 时，就为该基金产出了一个 DPI 和一个 IRR。

turns.en: Even though the asset is ongoing and the GP is still managing it, it has locked in DPI and IRR for the fund, even though the true value creation is not yet done.
turns.zh: 尽管资产还在持续经营、GP 仍在管理，基金的 DPI 和 IRR 已经锁定，而真正的价值创造还远没有完成。

turns.en: As a result, the GP's track record, arguably, is improved through this conflicted transaction. LPs can walk into our investment committee and present higher DPIs than perhaps our investment committee realizes.
turns.zh: 结果是，GP 的历史业绩可以说通过这宗冲突交易得到了改善。LP 走进我们的投资委员会时展示的 DPI，可能比我们投委会意识到的要高。

turns.en: We'll show it both ways. Actual DPI and DPI less, we call it synthetic. DPI, when it's a CV or an NAV loan, we'll strip all of that out. In an instance where you see a CV that you feel is a trophy asset, the classic asset that a GP wants to hold on for longer because it performs well and there's lots more to do.
turns.zh: 我们会两种方式都展示：实际 DPI，以及去掉——我们称之为——合成（synthetic）DPI。凡是涉及 CV 或 NAV 贷款（NAV loan）的，我们把这些全部剔除。——如果你看到一个 CV，你觉得它是一件奖杯资产（trophy asset），GP 因为业绩好、后续空间大而想长期持有的那种经典资产，

turns.en: When you go to re-underwrite a manager, if you've stripped that out as part of synthetic DPI, how do you think about the difference between that CV versus another CV that you might not feel strongly about the quality of the asset?
turns.zh: 当你去重新承做一个管理人时，如果你已经把那块从合成 DPI 里剔除了，你怎么看待那个 CV 和另一个你对资产质量不那么看好的 CV 之间的区别？

turns.en: We show full track record, which includes all the funds plus all the CVs when we walk into our investment committee. It's almost a no-win when we show the CV track record.
turns.zh: 我们走进投委会时展示的是完整的历史业绩，包括所有基金加上所有 CV。展示 CV 的业绩，几乎是怎么都不讨好。

turns.en: If you walk in with a CV track record that's too good, you would think they'd be excited because it is still an investment judgment and our investment committee is upset because they think if it did that well, they sold it for too cheap and therefore a fair process wasn't run.
turns.zh: 如果你带着特别亮眼的 CV 业绩进去，你可能以为大家会高兴，因为这毕竟也是投资判断——但投委会反而会不满，他们认为既然表现这么好，那就是卖得太便宜了，流程不公平。

turns.en: If you walk in with a bad CV track record, the investment committee says, what's wrong with this GP? They have bad investment judgment. Why did they continue to own this asset?
turns.zh: 如果你带着很差的 CV 业绩进去，投委会会问：这个 GP 怎么回事？他们的投资判断有问题，为什么还继续持有这个资产？

turns.en: There's not a CV track record that can win in terms of an investment committee. With that, by definition, CVs can't outperform too much. There are exceptions to the rule.
turns.zh: 在投委会面前，没有哪种 CV 业绩能赢。所以从定义上讲，CV 不可能太好——当然凡事有例外。

turns.en: The asset class as a whole, the subsector of CVs. If they start doing too well, LPs will stop allowing GPs to do these out of the original fund.
turns.zh: 就整个资产类别、CV 这个子板块而言：如果它们做得太好，LP 就会不再允许 GP 从原基金里做这些。

turns.en: If they start doing too poorly, LPs will stop funding the CV buyers. There's a healthy tension such that CVs by their nature can't be structurally too good.
turns.zh: 如果做得太差，LP 就会停止给 CV 的买方供钱。其中有一种健康的张力，使得 CV 本质上不可能结构性地太好，

turns.en: Also can't be structurally too bad. There's not much data on performance out there, but it's early. The data I've seen supports the types of the case.
turns.zh: 也不可能结构性地太坏。关于业绩的数据还不多，但毕竟还早，我见过的数据支持这种判断。

turns.en: Number seven, LPs are paying for an exit function that's no longer being performed. As LPs, we pay a GP by and large two and 20 to use the generic terms.
turns.zh: 第七个：LP 在为一项不再被履行的退出职能付钱。作为 LP，我们付给 GP 的，大体上是 2/20——用通用说法。

turns.en: What are we paying two and 24? There's three key judgment items that the GP does that we're paying for. The first is sourcing and evaluating investments.
turns.zh: 我们在 2/20 里付的是什么？GP 有三项关键判断是我们付钱买的。第一是项目的寻源与投资评估。

turns.en: The second is creating value in those investments. The third is exiting those investments. If you take CVs to their logical extreme and a GP CVs every asset in its fund, it's thrown its hands up on the third and said, I'm conflicted.
turns.zh: 第二是在这些投资中创造价值。第三是退出这些投资。如果把 CV 推到逻辑极致——GP 把基金里每个资产都装进 CV——那它就是在第三个环节摊手说：我有利益冲突，

turns.en: I can no longer make the exit determination. LP, it's your decision. That's fine, but I paid you GP to do three things. You're only doing two of those.
turns.zh: 我没法再做退出的判断了，LP，这是你的决定。可以，但我付钱给你是让你做三件事的，你现在只做两件了。

turns.en: That's frustrating because us limited partners are becoming less limited. We're not paying any less for taking the decision making back within our own teams.
turns.zh: 这令人沮丧，因为我们有限合伙人（limited partner）越来越'不有限'了。我们把决策权收回自己的团队，付的钱却一分没少。

turns.en: What's the potential to renegotiate that fee? This is one of those idealistic statements. I've yet to hear anyone say, that's unfair. It takes a long time to change markets.
turns.zh: 重新谈判这笔费用的可能性有多大？——这属于理想主义的说法之一。我还没听到有谁公开说这不公平。改变一个市场需要很长时间。

turns.en: There is an entire infrastructure built around the two and 20 model. I'm not sitting here proposing that we're going to change that overnight.
turns.zh: 围绕 2/20 模式已经建起了整套基础设施。我并不是坐在这里提议一夜之间改变它。

turns.en: It's more highlighting to a GP. Here's one of many reasons. It's a shifting of the discernment that an LP is paying a GP for. How about the last three?
turns.zh: 这更多是向 GP 点出来：这是众多原因之一，它正在转移 LP 付钱给 GP 所购买的那种判断力。——最后三条呢？

turns.en: Number eight, cannibalization of co-investment. Historically, if this asset had been sold to another GP, probably that other GP would have required some co-invest to do it.
turns.zh: 第八个：跟投的自我蚕食。历史上，如果这个资产卖给另一家 GP，那家 GP 多半会要求一些跟投额度。

turns.en: The market for buyout co-investment, at least in the US, is no fee, no carry. This has effectively been taken out of the co-invest pipeline.
turns.zh: 至少在美国，并购类跟投的市场是无费用、无 carry 的。这实际上被从跟投管道里抽走了。

turns.en: This is effectively cannibalizing fee free co-invest because now it's fee paying co-invest via a CV vehicle. LPs have built a lot of infrastructure up over the last couple of decades around building out co-invest teams.
turns.zh: 这实际上在蚕食零费用的跟投，因为现在变成了通过 CV 载体收费的跟投。过去二十来年，LP 围绕建立跟投团队搭建了大量基础设施。

turns.en: This is taking some of the deals out of the pipeline. Understandably, that's frustrating. Have you seen that in practice, that the co-investment top of the funnel is less than you would have thought?
turns.zh: 这正在把一些交易从管道里拿走，这种沮丧不难理解。——在实践中，你是否看到过跟投漏斗的顶部比你原本预期的更窄？

turns.en: I've seen a couple of things. First, deals that have gone into CVs, we know historically, we're not IPOs, we're not strategic candidates. They would have been sold to another sponsor.
turns.zh: 我见到了一些情况。首先，进入 CV 的那些交易，从历史上我们知道，它们不是 IPO 候选，也不是战略买家的候选，它们原本会卖给另一家财务买家。

turns.en: They would have been too big for that sponsor. That is absolutely happening. Some co-investments that I've heard from LPs when they're exiting alongside the fund, they might be allowed to reinvest, but it's via the CV at full fees.
turns.zh: 它们对那家买家来说原本会太大。这确确实实在发生。我也从一些 LP 那里听到，当他们跟随基金一起退出时，可能被允许重新投入，但只能通过 CV、按全额费用。

turns.en: Even if you had a co-invest in the original and the GP is gonna keep the asset through a CV, that fee free co-invest option is being taken away.
turns.zh: 即使你原来有跟投，而 GP 要通过 CV 继续持有那个资产，那个零费用的跟投选项也被拿走了。

turns.en: LPs are being forced to either exit what they had at no fee, no carry, or roll it into now a worse fee structure than they had before, full fees, full carry.
turns.zh: LP 被迫要么按原来的无费无 carry 退出，要么把它滚入一个比自己之前更差的收费结构：全额管理费、全额 carry。

turns.en: Number nine, reduction of right tail upside. These are often pitched as a GP's best assets. Oftentimes we'll see CVs created when an asset has reached a 3X or a 5X, maybe even a 7 or a 10X multiple within the fund.
turns.zh: 第九个：右尾上行收益的缩减。这些往往被包装成 GP 最好的资产。常见的情形是，当某项资产在基金里已经做到 3 倍或 5 倍，甚至 7 倍、10 倍回报时，就成立 CV。

turns.en: The GP says it's time to de-risk this fund and put it into a CV. That makes sense. However, most CVs I've seen are underwritten to at least another 2X.
turns.zh: GP 说是时候给基金去风险、把它放进 CV 了。这说得通。然而我见过的大多数 CV，承销目标至少又是一个 2 倍。

turns.en: This is an asset that was sold at a 5X out of the fund and is being underwritten at a 2X in a CV. Had that stay in the original fund, that would have been a 10X deal.
turns.zh: 这是一个在基金里以 5 倍卖出、又被按 2 倍承销的资产。如果它留在原基金里，那本可能是一个 10 倍的交易。

turns.en: That's the exact reason that LPs are and the private equity business is the ability to capture that right tail skew when these best performing assets get moved out of the system.
turns.zh: 而捕捉右尾偏态（right tail skew）的能力，恰恰是 LP 所在意的、也是私募股权这门生意的核心——当这些表现最好的资产被移出体系时，这种能力就受损了。

turns.en: That can be frustrating for an LP who doesn't get to benefit from that. The last on the list. The final one, number 10, is somewhat related to number nine.
turns.zh: 对没能从中受益的 LP 来说，这会令人沮丧。清单上最后一个。第 10 条，和第 9 条有点相关。

turns.en: If you take that last philosophy and you apply it across the whole industry, CVs could have downward pressure on private equity returns industry-wide.
turns.zh: 如果你把刚才那个逻辑放到整个行业层面，CV 可能对行业整体的私募股权回报造成下行压力。

turns.en: These best assets are being systematically taken out of commingled funds and moved into standalone CVs before their final exit and before the full value creation story is over.
turns.zh: 这些最好的资产正在被系统性从混合基金中抽出、移入独立的 CV——在最终退出之前，在完整的价值创造故事结束之前。

turns.en: The data suggests LPs are selling more than they're rolling. The LPs who are typically only exposed to the original fund are not getting the benefit of us higher outsized returns.
turns.zh: 数据显示，LP 卖出的比滚入的多。那些通常只接触原基金的 LP，享受不到这些超额回报。

turns.en: As you've laid out these 10, imagine some theoretical, most practical limitations of CVs. You're also actively managing this program that's gonna have these CVs landing on all your desk all the time.
turns.zh: 你把这十条列出来之后，可以想象 CV 在理论上最实际的一些限制。你同时也在积极管理着这样一个项目：这些 CV 会不断落到你的桌上。

turns.en: Knowing what you know about this, how have you chosen to participate in the market? We've chosen to participate in two ways. First, we sit on the advisory board of almost every fund that we invest in.
turns.zh: 了解这些之后，你选择了怎样参与这个市场？我们选择了两种方式参与。第一，我们几乎坐在所投每一期基金的咨询委员会（advisory board）上。

turns.en: We take a hands-on role as an advisory board member in terms of evaluating these CVs in order to waive the conflict. We've developed a scorecard internally that we fill out, has a GP done X, has a GP done Y.
turns.zh: 我们以咨询委员会成员的身份亲自参与 CV 的评估，以豁免利益冲突。我们在内部开发了一份记分卡，逐项填写：GP 做没做 X？GP 做没做 Y？

turns.en: If not, we vote no. The second thing is when we have the opportunity to roll or sell ourselves when the election notice comes out. We've taken the view that as long as it's over a certain size threshold, we have a $250 billion plan at Texas teachers.
turns.zh: 没做到，我们就投反对票。第二件事，是当我们自己收到滚入还是卖出的选择通知时。我们的观点是：只要超过一定的规模门槛——Texas Teachers 是一个 2500 亿美元的养老金——

turns.en: Some things are not enough capital to be a good use of time. When it's over a certain size threshold, we have to roll up our sleeves and dig in.
turns.zh: 有些事情资本量太小，就不值得投入时间。超过一定规模的，我们必须撸起袖子深入研究。

turns.en: We're evaluating the asset. We're evaluating the sponsor fit. All that's the same work as a co-investment. We're also evaluating the alignment.
turns.zh: 我们在评估资产、评估项目与 GP 的契合度——所有这些都和跟投的功课一样——同时我们还在评估利益对齐。

turns.en: That can be a lot harder to do. We'd have to effectively stop everything we're doing and evaluate it. We've also decided we have a large dedicated co-investment team.
turns.zh: 那可能难得多，我们得 effectively 放下手边的一切去评估它。我们还决定，既然我们有一个庞大的专职跟投团队，

turns.en: We've opened up the phone lines to be buyers of CVs that are beyond our roll-sell decisions. We're actively out there sourcing new deals and evaluating those.
turns.zh: 我们就敞开线路，去做那些超出我们滚入/卖出决策范围的 CV 的买方。我们在主动寻源新交易并评估它们。

turns.en: They do have a higher bar because they have fees associated with them relative to most of our co-invest deal flow, which is no fee, no carry.
turns.zh: 那些确实有更高的门槛，因为相比我们大多数无费无 carry 的跟投项目流，它们带有费用。

turns.en: We have a certain threshold upon which we might be willing to accept some fees in a CV if we like the asset. We've had to build on the resources, roll up our sleeves.
turns.zh: 我们有某个阈值，如果看好资产，我们愿意在 CV 里接受一些费用。我们不得不追加资源、卷起袖子干。

turns.en: We found no other way around it. To get a sense, within the CVs that come from your existing portfolio of managers that fit that minimum size threshold, what percentage of them would you say you end up investing or rolling in?
turns.zh: 我们没找到别的办法。——想了解一下：在来自你们现有管理人组合、符合最低规模门槛的 CV 里，最终有多大比例你们会投资或滚入？

turns.en: It's a number that we track. It's not a number that we publicize publicly. However, of the actionable deals we see, we call it a hit rate. How many do we do versus how many do we exit or sell?
turns.zh: 这是一个我们内部追踪的数字，不是对外公开的数字。不过，在我们看到的可操作交易中，我们把它叫命中率：我们做了多少，相比退出或卖出了多少？

turns.en: Our hit rate is no different in CV roll versus sell decisions as it is in actionable co-investment decisions. If we do one out of 10 co-invest, we probably do one out of 10 rolls.
turns.zh: 在 CV 的滚入还是卖出决策上，我们的命中率与可操作跟投决策的命中率没有两样。如果十个跟投我们做一个，十个滚入我们大概也做一个。

turns.en: We don't have a house of you that CVs are inherently good or bad, a great buy or a great sell. Interesting opportunities can exist, but you have to do the work.
turns.zh: 我们内部没有'CV 天然好或天然坏、天然是好买点或好卖点'的观点。有意思的机会可能存在，但你必须做功课。

turns.en: We're gonna take a quick break in the action to tell you about Brookfield. Brookfield invests in the thing behind the thing behind the next big thing.
turns.zh: 我们在精彩处插播一下，来介绍 Brookfield。Brookfield 投资于事物背后、再背后的下一个大事件。

turns.en: Their focus across infrastructure, energy, real estate, private equity and credit is helping to build the backbone of the global economy. Brookfield combines deep operational expertise with disciplined long-term investing, uncovering value and partnering alongside clients to shape tomorrow's economy today.
turns.zh: 他们在基础设施、能源、房地产、私募股权和信贷领域的专注布局，正在帮助构建全球经济的骨架。Brookfield 把深厚的运营专长与纪律严明的长期投资结合起来，发掘价值，与客户并肩，在此刻塑造明天的经济。

turns.en: Invest in the businesses that shape tomorrow. Learn how you can own what's next at Brookfield.com slash own. This is not an offer to sell or investment advice.
turns.zh: 投资塑造明天的企业。前往 Brookfield.com/own，了解如何拥有下一个。这不是出售证券的要约，也不是投资建议。

turns.en: Investing involves risk, including the loss of capital. And now, back to the show. So we take a step back from CVs as this fourth leg of a stool of how GPs are gonna get liquidity.
turns.zh: 投资有风险，包括可能损失本金。——现在回到节目。我们把 CV 当作 GP 获取流动性的四条凳子腿之一，往后退一步来看。

turns.en: We're still facing this liquidity bottleneck that's been around the last four or five years. How do you think this is playing out over the next couple of years?
turns.zh: 我们仍然面对过去四五年一直存在的流动性瓶颈。你怎么看未来几年这件事会如何演变？

turns.en: It's something we spend a lot of time thinking about. It's something we're concerned about. It brings me to a topic we haven't covered, but probably should, which is zombie funds.
turns.zh: 这是我们花了很多时间思考、也让我们担忧的问题。它把我带到一个我们还没谈过、但大概该谈的话题：僵尸基金（zombie fund）。

turns.en: A zombie fund is a fund that has stop making new deals, also can't raise capital. It's neither dead because the fund still has assets and it's not alive either because they're not adding to those assets and they have no more dry powder.
turns.zh: 僵尸基金是指停止做新交易、也募不到资的基金。它不算死，因为基金还有资产；它也不算活，因为不再增加资产，也没有更多的干火药（dry powder）。

turns.en: It's a zombie. We saw them a lot coming out of five years or so post financial crisis. The industry data suggests other LPs have the same view that these zombie funds are gonna become a real industry problem in the coming years.
turns.zh: 它就是个僵尸。金融危机后五年左右我们见过很多。行业数据显示，其他 LP 也有同样的判断：僵尸基金将在未来几年成为真正的行业问题。

turns.en: I saw a research report by Caller this summer come out and say that 54% of LPs expect the number of zombie funds in their portfolio two years from now to be higher.
turns.zh: 我今年夏天看到 Callan 发布的一份研究报告说，54% 的 LP 预期两年后他们组合中的僵尸基金数量会更多。

turns.en: Two years ago, that number was 28%. There's a structural vintage problem. The 2018 to 2022 vintages deployed capital in a low rate, high multiple environment.
turns.zh: 两年前，这个数字是 28%。这里有一个结构性的年份（vintage）问题：2018 到 2022 年份在低利率、高倍数的环境里部署了资本。

turns.en: They were not able to exit those deals in time. That environment no longer exists. The math doesn't work on exits. As a result, there's a structural DPI problem.
turns.zh: 他们没能及时退出那些交易，而那个环境已不复存在，退出的账算不过来。结果就是结构性的 DPI 问题。

turns.en: That backlog is gonna take years to work through the system. CVs are an interesting topic because you would think that they would solve the zombie problem.
turns.zh: 这个积压需要好几年才能在整个体系里消化。CV 是个有意思的话题，因为你可能会以为它们能解决僵尸问题。

turns.en: All CVs do is kick this can down the road. A CV can help an individual asset. It might help a single GP avoid being a zombie. There's far more stranded assets than there is capital for CVs.
turns.zh: 但 CV 所做的只是把这个罐子往前踢。CV 也许能帮助单项资产，也许能帮助某个 GP 避免变成僵尸。可搁浅资产的体量远大于可用于 CV 的资本。

turns.en: CVs alone will not solve the zombie problem. This cash becomes trapped, earning limited returns if any, you can't exit without selling in the secondary market at a significant discount.
turns.zh: 单靠 CV 解决不了僵尸问题。这些现金被困住，最多只有很低的回报，不通过二级市场大幅折价就退不出去。

turns.en: All the while, the economics are misaligned. A GP is collecting fees on NAV or on their cost basis that hasn't converted to cash in years. There's little incentive for them to force a sale because they may not be in the carry.
turns.zh: 与此同时，经济条款是错位的。GP 按 NAV 或按成本基础收费，而这些费用多年没有转化为现金。他们缺乏推动出售的动力，因为他们可能已经不在 carry 里。

turns.en: There may not be any more cash coming in when they sell. These funds are often amongst us LPs worst performers. They become a huge drag on your time from a governance perspective.
turns.zh: 卖出时也许不会再有新的现金进来。这些基金往往是我们 LP 表现最差的持仓，它们在治理层面大量占用我们的时间。

turns.en: Lots of amendments come our way. I don't have an answer to your question, Ted, on how the liquidity drought gets solved. It's gonna force some knock on effects such as zombie funds that are gonna start taking the mind share of us LPs and start to become a real frustrating topic for us all to deal with.
turns.zh: 很多修正案会送到我们面前。Ted，关于流动性枯竭如何解，我没有答案。它会逼出一些连锁反应，比如僵尸基金将开始占据 LP 的注意力，成为一个我们所有人都要面对的真正令人头疼的问题。

turns.en: What do you hear about the public markets, the IPO market as a potential exit path for private equity assets? Outside of a couple large scale growth capital names, we haven't seen a lot of activity in the public markets.
turns.zh: 关于公开市场——IPO 市场作为私募股权资产的潜在退出路径——你都听到些什么？——除了少数几个大型成长期标的，我们没有看到公开市场有太多动作。

turns.en: We're not encouraging our GPs to go and exit through the public markets because it can often be hard for them to fully exit. I call an IPO step one of a multi-step exit because rarely can you get full equity on day one.
turns.zh: 我们并不鼓励我们的 GP 通过公开市场退出，因为他们往往很难完全退出。我把 IPO 称为多步退出的第一步，因为很少有公司能在上市首日就把全部股权卖掉。

turns.en: The other big question in people's minds and private equity is what happens with private wealth, retail, retirement plan assets coming in. Wondering if you have any views of where we are today and where that might go in the future.
turns.zh: 人们心里关于私募股权的另一个大问题是：私人财富、零售、退休计划资金进来之后会怎么样？想知道你对现状以及未来走向有什么看法。

turns.en: This has been an emerging concern. SLPs are watching it closely. A lot of the top 10 concerns we just walked through on CVs are the exact same concerns LPs have on private wealth and retail capital.
turns.zh: 这是一个新兴的担忧，LP 都在密切观察。我们刚才讲 CV 的前十大担忧，其中很多恰恰是 LP 对私人财富和零售资本的担忧。

turns.en: Some of the same ones are dilution of the GP's time and attention, dilution of the alignment because of this new fee stream, co-invest cannibalization.
turns.zh: 其中几个是相同的：GP 时间和注意力的稀释、因新费用收入造成的利益对齐稀释、跟投的自我蚕食。

turns.en: What's interesting about retail capital, it's a unique wrinkle to this versus CVs. There's a saying out there that I like, which is private equity for the retail investors, the right strategy, but the wrong structure.
turns.zh: 零售资本有意思的地方在于，相比 CV 它有一个独特的褶皱。有一句外面的说法我很喜欢：对零售投资人来说，私募股权是对的策略、错的结构。

turns.en: Institutional investors, people like Texas teachers and retail investors, people like myself, my parents 401K plan, we have different risk profiles, liquidity needs, time horizons, performance expectations, level of expertise and resources.
turns.zh: 机构投资者——像 Texas Teachers 这样的——和零售投资人——比如我自己、我父母的 401K 计划——有着不同的风险画像、流动性需求、时间跨度、业绩预期、专业水平和资源。

turns.en: Yet a retail product oftentimes, those retail investors are being placed in the exact same assets side by side with an institutional investor.
turns.zh: 然而在零售产品里，这些零售投资人往往被放进和机构投资者完全一样的资产，并肩而立。

turns.en: One of private equity's advantages over public markets was that companies can't stay focused on the longterm. Putting these into a semi-liquid, quarterly redemption vehicle takes away that longterm horizon.
turns.zh: 私募股权相比公开市场的优势之一，是企业可以专注于长期。把这些资产放进半流动、季度赎回的载体里，就夺走了那种长期视角。

turns.en: Illiquidity is a feature, not a bug of the private equity asset class. You're taking away that feature in my opinion when you put it into a semi-liquid structure.
turns.zh: 非流动性是私募股权资产类别的一个特性（feature），不是缺陷（bug）。在我看来，放进半流动结构里就剥夺了这个特性。

turns.en: What are some of the other things you have your eyes on? Within retail, the things that we care about in addition to some of the top 10 items, we're paying a lot of attention to hard caps and sharing percentage.
turns.zh: 你还有哪些关注的事情？——在零售领域，除了前十大项里的一些，我们非常关注硬性上限（hard cap）和共用比例：

turns.en: How much can a commingled fund share with a retail vehicle alongside it? If I go into a $10 billion fund, I'm not paying attention to the LPA.
turns.zh: 一只混合基金能和与它并行的零售载体共用多少？如果我投了一只 100 亿美元的基金，而我没有注意 LPA——

turns.en: If that LPA allows a retail vehicle to invest infinite amounts, then I've effectively signed up for an uncapped fund. Fund size is a key underwriting of SLPs.
turns.zh: 如果那份 LPA 允许零售载体投入无限量，那我实际上签的就是一只无上限的基金。基金规模是 LP 承做的关键要素之一，

turns.en: Knowing how much they can invest is a key care about. Another one is, how does the investment timing work? Are both the retail and the institutional fund required to buy and sell at the same time?
turns.zh: 知道他们最多能投多少是我们关注的核心。另一个是投资的时点如何运作：零售基金和机构基金是否被要求同时买入、同时卖出？

turns.en: Can one buy and sell to the other? Can one sell before the other? Their inherent conflicts, different risk tolerances, liquidity needs between two different investors.
turns.zh: 能不能一方买入、另一方卖给对方？能不能一方先于另一方卖出？这中间天然存在冲突——两类不同投资者之间的风险容忍度和流动性需求不同。

turns.en: Finally, is this cannibalizing our co-invest opportunity? We're spending a lot of time thinking about these things. So far, most of the activity, to the extent there is activity on the retail side with private equity is started with the large, mostly public alternative asset managers.
turns.zh: 最后，这是否在蚕食我们的跟投机会？我们花了很多时间思考这些问题。到目前为止，零售端私募股权的活动——如果说有的话——大多是由大型、多为上市的另类资产管理人发起的。

turns.en: I'm curious if you've seen traction below that top tier of half a dozen firms. We haven't seen a lot start to raise products. When I talk with a lot of our GPs, if you catch them in a moment of truth and transparency, they would say they're certainly thinking about it.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，在那前六家这个层级之下，你是否看到过实质进展？——我没看到太多人开始募集产品。当我和很多 GP 交谈，如果你在一个说真话的坦诚时刻捕捉到他们，他们会承认肯定在琢磨这件事。

turns.en: Met with a large publicly traded CEO recently, this individual said, sure, I'm glad I'm CEO of a large firm and not a small firm right now because of the strength of consolidation that this large cap manager has.
turns.zh: 最近我见到一位大型上市公司 CEO，这位仁兄说：我很庆幸现在是大型公司的 CEO 而不是小公司的 CEO，因为这种大型管理人所带来的整合力量。

turns.en: I'm not sure that it's coming immediately to the middle market. However, eventually, if it continues to grow, large cap players will want middle market offerings for their retail investors.
turns.zh: 我不确定它会很快来到中型市场（middle market）。但迟早，如果这个趋势继续增长，大型管理人会想要为他们的零售投资人提供中型市场的产品。

turns.en: They'll need distribution channels, a pipeline of assets to take advantage of the new capital coming in that has appetite for smaller deals.
turns.zh: 他们需要分销渠道、需要资产管道，来利用那些对较小交易有 Appetite 的新资本。

turns.en: You may see joint ventures, you may see consolidation of GPs, you may see the big buying the smaller. So while it's not there now, there's a world in which it could be far more prevalent for middle market GPs down the road.
turns.zh: 你可能会看到合资，看到 GP 的整合，看到大鱼吃小鱼。所以虽然现在还没到那一步，但存在一个未来的世界，中型市场 GP 会更普遍地卷入其中。

turns.en: What's changed in the last few years and how you've gone about investing in the space? We're spending a lot more time now than we would have on a couple of areas.
turns.zh: 过去几年里什么变了？你们在这个领域的投资方式有什么不同？——我们现在在几个方面花的时间远比过去多。

turns.en: One is we're underwriting the unrealized portfolio more deeply than we had in the past. It was easy to assume when markets were up into the right that a deal held at cost would get to 2X.
turns.zh: 一个是我们对未变现组合做比过去更深度的承做。过去市场一路上行的时候，很容易假设一个按成本持有的交易最终会到 2 倍。

turns.en: That's harder to assume now. We're spending a lot of time understanding what was the multiple paid for this portfolio? How has EBITDA traded?
turns.zh: 现在这种假设更难成立。我们花大量时间弄清楚：这个组合付的倍数是多少？EBITDA 表现如何？

turns.en: How has revenue performed since entry? What is the actual versus budget on a year by year asset by asset basis? Where does leverage sit today?
turns.zh: 入场以来收入表现如何？逐年、逐资产的实际 versus 预算是什么情况？当前的杠杆水平如何？

turns.en: We've even gone out and looked at where are the portfolio's credits trading? What do the public credit investors think about the quality of this portfolio?
turns.zh: 我们甚至出去看了组合的债权在什么价位交易——公开市场的债权投资人怎么看这个组合的质量？

turns.en: Where are the secondary bids for the LP interest trading? There's a lot less liquidity, a lot less distributions. There's a lot larger unrealized portfolio to get your arms around.
turns.zh: LP 权益的二手报价现在处于什么水平？流动性少了很多，分配少了很多，未变现组合的规模大了得多，需要你花力气去把握。

turns.en: In addition to a deeper analysis of the unrealized portfolio, we're spending a lot of time evaluating the partnership. This is hard to do. We're assessing, is this a partnership that is gonna stick together when the going gets tough?
turns.zh: 除了对未变现组合更深入的分析，我们花大量时间评估合伙人关系（partnership）。这很难做到。我们在判断：这是一个在艰难时刻仍能抱团挺过去的合伙人团队吗？

turns.en: It's easy for the partners to work well, look past shortcomings, not get on each other's nerves when all is going great and Kerry's getting paid.
turns.zh: 当一切顺风顺水、carry 照拿不误的时候，合伙人们很容易相处融洽、对彼此的短处睁一只眼闭一只眼、不互相惹恼。

turns.en: All that our GPs really have as assets are the people. Any cracks in those partnerships start to come through when someone's deal starts to underperform or maybe they're not gonna get Kerry or maybe the next fund isn't gonna be quite as big as they thought it was gonna be or they have to start letting some people go.
turns.zh: 我们的 GP 真正拥有的资产就是人。当某个人的交易开始表现不佳，或者他可能拿不到 carry，或者下一期基金没有想象中那么大，或者不得不开始裁掉一些人的时候，这些合伙人团队的裂缝就开始显现。

turns.en: Hard to do, but we're spending a lot of time thinking through partnership dynamics. A lot of these partnerships haven't been tested. The last 10, 15 years have been good times for the private equity industry.
turns.zh: 很难做到，但我们花了很多时间思考合伙人动态。很多这些合伙人团队还没有被真正考验过。过去 10 到 15 年对私募股权行业来说是好时光。

turns.en: A lot of these firms were started over that time. Hard to do, but an important part of our underwriting. How do you go about getting underneath?
turns.zh: 很多公司就是在那段时间里成立的。虽然难，但这也是我们承做的重要一环。——你们是怎么探到水面之下的？

turns.en: No one has an incentive from the GP side to let you know that there's a fracture underneath. It's much more an art than a science. It's one of the reasons I love being an LP.
turns.zh: GP 那边没有人有动力让你知道水面下有裂缝。这更多是一门艺术而不是科学。这也是我热爱做 LP 的原因之一。

turns.en: I like to say LPs have both quantitative tools and qualitative tools that they have to bring to bear because at the end of the day, all we're doing is assessing is this a person that I can trust with the teachers of Texas money?
turns.zh: 我喜欢说，LP 必须同时动用定量工具和定性工具，因为说到底，我们评估的就一件事：这个人值不值得托付 Teachers of Texas 的钱？

turns.en: Do I think they'll make good decisions? It's almost a cycle analysis exam. You have to dig in. How did that person show up in the diligence session?
turns.zh: 我觉得他会做出好的决策吗？这几乎就是一场周期分析考试。你必须深挖：那个人在尽调会上的状态如何？

turns.en: Did you see any body language that was a little concerning? Had there been departures? How do you talk to those departures? Some more reference calls than we've ever done before.
turns.zh: 你有没有注意到任何让人略感不安的肢体语言？有没有人员离职？你怎么去联系那些离职的人？我们做了比以往任何时候都多的背景调查电话。

turns.en: The importance of an onsite, visiting them in their office, in their element. Anyone can fly to Texas and look great in our office for a couple of hours.
turns.zh: 现场拜访（onsite）的重要性：去他们的办公室、在他们的主场看他们。任何人都可以飞到奥斯汀，在我们的办公室里神采奕奕几个小时。

turns.en: Maybe it's a different story if we show up in their office and spend an entire day, plus maybe a dinner. There's lots of little tricks and little tools, but it's a culmination of all of the soft stuff.
turns.zh: 但如果我们出现在他们的办公室，待上一整天，再加一顿晚餐，情况可能就不一样了。有很多小技巧、小工具，但最终这是所有软性信息的汇总。

turns.en: The quantitative is still important, but we're spending a time coming up with that art project of how do we assess the qualitative side of these partnerships?
turns.zh: 定量的东西仍然重要，但我们正在花时间打磨那门'艺术'：如何评估这些合伙人团队定性的一面？

turns.en: How do you get conviction if you detect something doesn't feel great, but you're not sure and it is qualitative? That's what I love, that's investing.
turns.zh: 如果你察觉某些地方不太对劲、但又不确切，而且它属于定性层面，你怎么建立确信度？

turns.en: It's easy when there's no hair, it's an easy story, track record's been great, we teach our team all the time, trust your gut. If there's one tool that we have, it's a matrix where on the X axis is attractiveness of return, on the Y axis is risk.
turns.zh: 这就是我热爱的地方，这就是投资。当没有疑点、故事简单、历史业绩出色时，决定很容易——我们一直教导团队：相信直觉。如果说我们有一个工具，那它是一个矩阵：X 轴是回报吸引力，Y 轴是风险。

turns.en: If I have a manager where there's a high level of risk because of complexity, turnover, change in strategy, high growth and fun size, et cetera, but they're an N of one type manager that I've been trying to get access to, that's the top right quadrant.
turns.zh: 如果我有一个管理人，因为复杂性、人员流失、策略变动、基金规模的高速增长等原因而风险水平偏高，但它是那种我一直在设法获取的 N 中取一（N of one）型管理人——那就落在右上象限。

turns.en: We have long discussions about those, we may be more willing to lean in to that risk because there's nowhere else that we can replicate that potential return.
turns.zh: 我们会就这类情况展开长时间讨论，我们可能更愿意朝那种风险倾斜，因为没有别的地方能复制那个潜在回报。

turns.en: If it's a manager that we feel is a little lower in our conviction, maybe is similarly situated with a couple of other managers in our portfolio, they're a little lower down the return side of the spectrum, but they're high on the risk side, that's where we typically say we can recreate this return stream somewhere else with less risk.
turns.zh: 如果是一个我们确信度略低的管理人，在我们的组合里可能有几家情况和它类似，它在回报这一侧稍低一些，但风险偏高——那通常我们会说：这个回报流我们可以在别处用更低的风险复制。

turns.en: As you built this portfolio over 16 years to where it is today in the 30 billions, where do you think it goes the next couple years? We certainly don't think growth of our team is gonna happen as fast as it has, maybe we continue to grow a little bit.
turns.zh: 你花了 16 年把这个组合建到 300 多亿美元的今天，你觉得未来几年它会走向哪里？——我们肯定不认为团队的增长会像过去那么快，也许会继续小幅增长。

turns.en: We have a London presence, that was a large growth area, I'm not sure there's any new geographic offices on our horizon. We've studied secondaries and while we might do a little bit here and there, it's not a area of focus for us in terms of a new team build down.
turns.zh: 我们有了伦敦的据点，那是很大的一块增长区域，我不确定我们接下来还有新的地区办公室。我们研究过二手份额（secondaries），虽然这里那里可能会做一点，但它不是我们在组建新团队上的重点领域。

turns.en: In the past, we were creating alpha by entering into new markets, whether that be co-invest, large strategic partnerships, better fee savings, our CIO likes to say it's now all about craftsmanship alpha, which is fine-tuning the processes we've developed, making small changes to try to produce better results.
turns.zh: 过去，我们通过进入新市场创造 alpha——无论是跟投、大型战略合作伙伴，还是更好的费用节约。我们的 CIO 喜欢说，现在关键是匠心 alpha（craftsmanship alpha）：微调我们已经建立起来的流程，做出小的改变，力争更好的结果。

turns.en: The alpha is coming through a larger team that can go source more transactions, build deeper relationships, have more knowledge, try to deploy more on the AI front, use all the tools that we've developed in our toolkit.
turns.zh: Alpha 来自一个更大的团队：去寻源更多交易、建立更深关系、拥有更多知识，在 AI 方面尝试更多部署，用好我们工具箱里发展出来的所有工具。

turns.en: I'm not sure that it's gonna be revolutionary, probably more evolutionary. Scott Norm, make sure I get a chance to ask you a couple of closing questions.
turns.zh: 我不确定这会是革命性的，更可能是演化式的。——Scott，一定让我有机会问你几个收尾的问题。

turns.en: What was your first paid job and what did you learn from it? My first paid job, I was probably 13 years old. I'm not even sure if that's a legal working age.
turns.zh: 你的第一份有偿工作是什么？你从中学到了什么？我的第一份有偿工作，大概是 13 岁的时候。我甚至不确定那是不是合法的打工年龄。

turns.en: I was a day camp counselor for a kid's summer camp in my neighborhood. I have the benefit of having excellent role models and my parents who both had full-time jobs.
turns.zh: 我在社区里一个儿童夏令营当日间营辅导员。我很幸运，父母都有全职工作，是我的优秀榜样。

turns.en: I learned at an early age. During my summers, during my winter breaks, I could be productive and earn a paycheck. My mom always had me working.
turns.zh: 我很小就懂得：在我的暑假、我的寒假里，我可以既做有意义的事又挣到工资。我妈一直让我干活。

turns.en: I learned all the things you learn around executive functioning. I had to get myself to work on time. I had to get myself home from work. I rode my bike.
turns.zh: 我学到了所有关于执行功能（executive functioning）的东西：我得自己按时到工作地点，得自己从工作地点回家，我骑自行车。

turns.en: I had to learn, do I need a lunch today? Is this a swim day? How do I pack the appropriate items? I also learned that small acts of initiative go a long way to impressing a boss, especially amongst 13-year-olds.
turns.zh: 我还得琢磨：今天需不需要带午饭？今天是游泳日吗？我该怎么打包合适的物品？我也学到，小小的主动性很能打动老板，尤其在一群 13 岁的孩子中间。

turns.en: All it took was showing up a little early, offering to set up the cones for the soccer game, staying a little late and picking up the balls, looking around and saying, how can I be helpful?
turns.zh: 要做的不过是早到一点，主动帮忙摆足球游戏的锥桶，晚走一点把球收好，环顾四周问一句：我能帮上什么忙？

turns.en: Small acts went a long way. Which two people met the biggest impact on your professional life? Maybe instead of two people, I'll cop out a little and say which two organizations.
turns.zh: 小小的举动作用很大。——哪两个人对你的职业生涯影响最大？也许我不说两个人，稍微取个巧，说说两个组织吧。

turns.en: It's Alpenvest and Texas Teachers, the two LPs that I've worked for. I started my LP career at Alpenvest. It was an incredible place to learn.
turns.zh: 是 AlpInvest 和 Texas Teachers——我服务过的两家 LP。我的 LP 生涯始于 AlpInvest，那是一个学习的好地方。

turns.en: I invested across a full cycle, both the peak and the trough, worked with an incredible group of people, a lot of whom have gone on to be true leaders in the LP private equity space.
turns.zh: 我跨越整个周期投资，经历过顶峰也经历过谷底，与一群出色的人共事，他们中很多人后来成了 LP 私募股权领域真正的领导者。

turns.en: It's an incredible network that I developed and incredible skills. It was a special place to be and a special time in my life. The second organization is the one I'm at now, Texas Teachers.
turns.zh: 我从中建立了了不起的人脉、练就了了不起的技能。那是一段特别的时光、一个特别的地方。第二个组织就是我现在所在的 Texas Teachers。

turns.en: I never would have imagined when I moved back to Austin to work for Texas Teachers that here we sit 16 and a half years later, never would have imagined what it had turned into.
turns.zh: 当年我搬回奥斯汀为 Texas Teachers 工作时，绝没想过 16 年半后我们会站在这里，绝没想过它变成了今天的样子。

turns.en: Never would have imagined the life that my wife and I were able to create in Texas. It gave me not just a job, but a career. I'm eternally grateful for that opportunity.
turns.zh: 绝没想过我和妻子能在德州创造这样的生活。它给我的不仅是一份工作，而是一份事业。我对那个机会永远心怀感激。

turns.en: What's the best advice you've ever received? There's two pieces of advice that I've received that are in slight tension with each other. And I've had to be okay with that.
turns.zh: 你收到过的最好的建议是什么？——有两条建议，它们之间带点微妙的张力，我必须学会与这种张力相处。

turns.en: The first is my dad would always say, anything worth doing is worth doing right. I'll never forget as a high schooler, know it all, wanting to cut corners, wanting to take shortcuts.
turns.zh: 第一条是我爸总说：凡是值得做的事，就值得做好。我永远不会忘记，高中时那个自以为是的我，总想抄近道、想偷懒。

turns.en: Every time I would try to say, it's okay, I can cut the corner here. I'd hear my dad's voice pop up in my head. Anything worth doing, son, is worth doing right.
turns.zh: 每次我心里嘀咕'这里偷个懒没关系吧'，我爸的声音就会在我脑海里响起：孩子，凡是值得做的事，都值得做到位。

turns.en: Then I would do it fully and wholly as I knew I was supposed to as my dad taught me. And an old boss of mine used to say, don't let perfect get in the way of good enough.
turns.zh: 然后我就会照他教我的，完完整整、彻彻底底地去做。我的一位老老板则常说：别让完美挡住'足够好'的路。

turns.en: Not conflicted with anything worth doing is worth doing right. I've had to come to terms that both of those can be true. You wanna talk about how you reconcile that conflict?
turns.zh: 这和'凡是值得做的事都值得做好'并不冲突。我已经慢慢接受：这两句可以同时为真。——你想谈谈你怎么调和这个冲突吗？

turns.en: Life is about knowing when you need to be perfect and when you need to be good enough. That's been a lesson that I've had to learn over my years, which is when does the incremental effort produce no incremental return?
turns.zh: 人生就是要知道什么时候需要做到完美、什么时候足够好就行。这是我这些年必须学会的一课：什么时候额外的努力不再产生额外的回报？

turns.en: When is that incremental effort the most important effort you put out to produce the full return? That's not easy. Scott, last one. What life lesson have you learned that you wish you knew a lot earlier in life?
turns.zh: 什么时候那份额外的努力恰恰是产出全部回报的最重要努力？这并不容易。——Scott，最后一个问题。你人生中学到的、恨不得更早明白的一课是什么？

turns.en: One of my favorite analogies of life is that life is just the juggling of balls. In my life, I think of having five main balls that I'm juggling at all times.
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的一个人生的类比是：人生就是抛接一堆球。在我的人生里，我想我一直在同时抛接五个主要的球。

turns.en: Work, family, friends, faith, and health. Some of those balls are rubber balls. If you drop them, they bounce right back up, no problem. Some of those balls are glass balls.
turns.zh: 工作、家庭、朋友、信念、健康。其中一些球是橡胶球：掉了，它会自己弹回来，没问题。有些球是玻璃球。

turns.en: You drop them, they're shattered. They're ruined and irreconcilable. Life is all about knowing what balls are you juggling at what time and which ones are rubber and which ones are glass.
turns.zh: 你一松手，它们就碎了，毁了，不可挽回。人生的关键，就是知道你在什么时候抛接的是哪些球，哪些是橡胶球、哪些是玻璃球。

turns.en: Scott, thanks so much for sharing your insight. I appreciate it. Great to be here with you, Ted. Thanks for listening all the way to the end.
turns.zh: Scott，非常感谢你分享你的洞见，我很受益。——很高兴和你聊，Ted。——感谢各位一路听到底。

turns.en: If you made it this far, how about one ask for me? Tell one friend about the show. It's the best way to keep growing this incredible community.
turns.zh: 既然你们听到了这里，能不能帮我一个忙？把你的一个朋友介绍给我们的节目，这是让这个了不起的社群继续壮大的最好方式。

turns.en: Thanks so much. And until the next one, stay curious and keep compounding knowledge, relationships, and capital a little bit at a time. All opinions expressed by Ted and podcast guests are solely their own opinions and do not reflect the opinion of capital allocators or their firms.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。下一期再会之前，保持好奇，持续复利——知识、人脉和资本，一次一点点。Ted 和播客嘉宾表达的所有观点都仅是他们本人的观点，不代表 Capital Allocators 或其所在机构的观点。
